correctness.rationale: Hypergeometric indicator counting gives F_a(m)=Σ_i a_i C(N−a_i,m−1)/C(N,m). Independent exact Fraction computation over every 66 positive-integer partitions N=1..8 found the per-N 0/1/2-strict-peak counts (1,0,0),(2,0,0),(2,1,0),(4,1,0),(5,2,0),(6,5,0),(7,8,0),(12,9,1). Sole N=8 double peak is (5,2,1) at m=2,6 with (1,17/14,33/28,8/7,65/56,33/28,9/8,1). The proof derives exact adjacent ratio for all equal-abundance samples, permitting at most one turning point, and F(m)=tm/N+2rm(N−m)/(N(N−1)) for abundances in {1,2}, concave for all N. The finite census is exhaustive via integer partitions and independently evaluated subsets; only the symbolic contrasts cover arbitrary N.
residual_risks: Entire census ends at total N=8; no bound on number of peaks for larger heterogeneous censuses.
Without-replacement distinguishable individuals; strict integer interior peaks only; cannot extrapolate to variance or empirical stochastic trajectories.

value.rationale: Singleton counts are basic rarefaction and undersampling diagnostics.
